page: Microsoft Azure D128alds_v7 is a high-vCPU server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, delivering 128 dedicated virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system supports advanced instructions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside AES and SHA cryptographic accelerations. Memory is provisioned at 256 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 7559 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, while containing zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top tier for CPU, memory, and data throughput metrics. It achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 233,738.78 and a PassMark CPU score of 134,326.25. Memory bandwidth reaches 376.33 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 197.42 GB/sec for writes. The platform demonstrated 200.09 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, 823.88 GB/sec during multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and static web serving throughput of 105.54 GB/sec. On CPU-based inference workloads, it handled 331.9 prompt tokens per second and 66.04 generation tokens per second using a 7B model.

The 1:2 memory-to-core allocation offers cost-efficient scaling for compute-heavy workloads that do not demand large RAM footprints per thread. However, the relatively lean memory capacity per core acts as a tradeoff for large in-memory databases. Given the high clock rate and large NVMe SSD disk volume, the D128alds_v7 is well aligned with compute-intensive batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, high-throughput web serving, and database tasks that utilize fast local storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D128alds_v7 is an AMD EPYC 9V45 instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it incorporates 256 GB of system memory (2 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 7559 GB NVMe SSD local drive with Premium Storage support. The configuration omits discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across compute and memory workloads, scoring 134,326.25 on PassMark CPU, 200.09 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, and 823.88 GB/s on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block memory bandwidth exceeds 376 GB/s for reads and 197 GB/s for writes. While the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio requires careful sizing for RAM-heavy applications, the server delivers high cost efficiency for compute-intensive tasks, parallel compilation pipelines, high-throughput static web serving, and fast I/O local database operations.
